bridge: You described your entire life without using the word 'enjoy' once. Was that deliberate, or did you just notice?

sampleAnswers.questionText: How do you feel about your work right now?
Describe a real Tuesday. Not ideal. Real.
sampleAnswers.text: Wake at 7:30, check Slack in bed, standup, three status meetings, fix decks until 8pm, eat delivery on the couch, scroll until midnight.

bridge: The things that make you feel most alive are the things you've stopped making time for. What replaced them, and why did you let it?

sampleAnswers.questionText: Think about the last three times you had genuine fun. What were you doing?
sampleAnswers.text: Cooking for six friends from scratch, sketching street corners in my notebook, long cycling rides at 6am — all more than a year ago.

sampleAnswers.questionText: What activities outside work make you feel most alive?
sampleAnswers.text: Making things with my hands, though lately weekends disappear into catching up on email and errands.

bridge: You listed five worlds where you performed. Then whispered the one where you were real. Why does the real one get the smallest voice?

sampleAnswers.questionText: Which world (school, work, social) felt most like you? Which was the biggest performance?
sampleAnswers.text: College placements, work leadership reviews, alumni dinners, LinkedIn, and extended-family weddings are all performances. Maybe late-night talks with my sister felt slightly like me.

bridge: You want to disappear from the performances. But you still want to be seen. Just not like this. What would 'being seen right' actually look like?

sampleAnswers.questionText: Rank these: autonomy, mastery, impact, recognition, belonging.
Does prestige feel good, or just useful?
sampleAnswers.text: Useful as armor so nobody questions me, exhausting to maintain, yet I still care if people respect my craft.

bridge: What if the answer was never a career? What if it was a life, and the work just had to fit inside it?

sampleAnswers.questionText: Describe your ideal Monday morning. First three hours. Specific.
sampleAnswers.text: Sunlight on a quiet table, coffee without notifications, walking to a small workshop, two hours writing or building before talking to anyone.

bridge: I notice you described rest as something you earn, not something you deserve. Where did that belief start?

sampleAnswers.questionText: What activities outside work make you feel most alive?
sampleAnswers.text: Reading novels in the afternoon, though I only allow myself to do it once I've cleared every task and earned the downtime.

bridge: Isn't it true that you keep taking these projects because you're afraid of disappointing everyone?
Don't you think your people-pleasing is what really keeps your Tuesdays so crowded?
Wouldn't you say you're using gratitude to hide how resentful you actually feel?
Deep down, aren't you really scared of what happens if nobody needs you?
